subject: Science
text: Which of the following sequences correctly represents the sequence of biochemical steps in the nitrogen cycle in nature?
explanation: The nitrogen cycle consists of: Nitrogen fixation (atmospheric to compounds) \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen assimilation (taken up by plants) \\(\\rightarrow\\) Ammonification (decomposition to ammonia) \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrification (ammonia to nitrates) \\(\\rightarrow\\) Denitrification (nitrates back to gaseous nitrogen).

options.text: Nitrogen fixation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Ammonification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen assimilation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Denitrification
Nitrogen fixation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen assimilation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Ammonification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Denitrification
Ammonification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen fixation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Denitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen assimilation
Nitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Ammonification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Denitrification \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen fixation \\(\\rightarrow\\) Nitrogen assimilation

subject: Science
text: Food grains are thoroughly dried in the sun before storage. Why is a high moisture content in stored grains highly detrimental to their quality and preservation?
explanation: Moisture creates an ideal environment for fungi, bacteria, and insects to multiply, which spoils the grains, reduces their germination capacity, and leads to enzymatic degradation.

options.text: Moisture promotes the growth of fungi, bacteria, and pests, destroying germination capacity and spoiling grains
Moisture causes the grains to merge and fuse together into a single large block
Moisture reacts chemically with grain starch to produce toxic carbon monoxide gas
Moisture increases the weight of the grains, making them explode under high pressure

subject: Science
text: Why are antibiotics ineffective against viral diseases like influenza or COVID-19, whereas they are highly effective against bacterial infections?
explanation: Antibiotics target bacterial cell walls, protein synthesis, or specific bacterial metabolic pathways. Viruses do not possess these structures or pathways, relying instead on the host cell's machinery.

options.text: Because viruses are too small to be physically blocked by chemical molecules
Because viruses lack cell walls and their own metabolic pathways, which are the targets of antibiotics
Because antibiotics are neutralized by the acidic envelope of viruses
Because viruses reproduce only inside red blood cells, which antibiotics cannot enter

subject: Science
text: Sodium benzoate and sodium metabisulphite are commonly used food preservatives in jams and squashes. What is their primary biochemical mechanism of action?
explanation: These chemical preservatives release compounds (like benzoic acid or sulphur dioxide) that lower pH and inhibit cellular respiration and enzymatic activity in spoilage microbes.

options.text: They absorb all light falling on the food to prevent photo-oxidation
They create conditions that inhibit microbial growth and metabolic activities
They chemically convert sugars into indigestible complex starches
They sterilize the food by producing high-intensity heat locally

subject: Science
text: If a species of plant or animal is declared 'extinct in the wild' by conservation organizations, what does it mean?
explanation: Extinct in the wild means a species no longer exists in its natural habitat and is only known to survive in captivity, botanical gardens, or controlled breeding facilities.

options.text: The species has completely died out and no living individuals exist anywhere
The species survives only in captivity, cultivation, or controlled human care
The species has migrated to another continent and changed its habits
The species has been cloned and reintroduced into municipal parks

subject: Science
text: The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve contains diverse conservation zones. Which combination of national parks and wildlife sanctuaries is located within this biosphere reserve?
explanation: The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve consists of one national park named Satpura National Park, and two wildlife sanctuaries named Bori Sanctuary and Pachmarhi Sanctuary.

options.text: Satpura National Park, Bori Sanctuary, and Pachmarhi Sanctuary
Jim Corbett National Park, Gir Sanctuary, and Kaziranga Sanctuary
Kaziranga National Park, Sundarbans Sanctuary, and Bori Sanctuary
Satpura National Park, Kanha Sanctuary, and Bharatpur Sanctuary

subject: Science
text: In human reproduction, what is the role of the acrosome, located at the front tip of the sperm cell head, during fertilization?
explanation: The acrosome contains specialized enzymes that break down the outer protective layer (zona pellucida) of the ovum, enabling the sperm nucleus to enter and fuse with the egg nucleus.

options.text: It provides energy to the tail for swimming towards the ovum
It carries the genetic chromosomes from the father
It releases enzymes to digest the outer protective layers of the egg cell
It prevents other sperm cells from entering the uterus

subject: Science
text: Dolly the sheep was the first mammal successfully cloned. From which ewe was the nucleus taken, and which ewe gave birth to Dolly?
explanation: Dolly's nucleus was taken from a Finn Dorsett ewe's mammary gland and inserted into an enucleated egg from a Scottish Blackface ewe. The surrogate mother ewe was also a Scottish Blackface, but Dolly was genetically identical to the Finn Dorsett.

options.text: Nucleus from Scottish Blackface; surrogate mother was Finn Dorsett
Nucleus from Finn Dorsett; surrogate mother was Scottish Blackface
Nucleus from Finn Dorsett; surrogate mother was Finn Dorsett
Nucleus and egg both from Scottish Blackface; no surrogate mother

subject: Science
text: Which hormone, endocrine gland, and associated medical condition are correctly matched?
explanation: Growth hormone is secreted by the pituitary gland, and its deficiency during childhood causes dwarfism.

options.text: Insulin — Thyroid gland — Goitre
Growth hormone — Pituitary gland — Dwarfism
Thyroxine — Adrenal gland — Diabetes
Adrenaline — Pancreas — Gigantism

subject: Science
text: During puberty, which hormones secreted by the pituitary gland play the primary role in stimulating the production of testosterone in boys and estrogen in girls?
explanation: Gonadotropins (specifically LH and FSH) secreted by the pituitary gland stimulate the testes in males to produce testosterone, and the ovaries in females to produce estrogen.

options.text: Thyroxine and Adrenaline
Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing hormone (LH)
Insulin and Glucagon
Growth hormone and Melatonin

subject: Science
text: Coal is classified into different ranks based on its carbon content. Arrange Peat, Lignite, Bituminous, and Anthracite in increasing order of carbon percentage.
explanation: Peat has the lowest carbon content (< 60%). Lignite is next (60-70%), followed by Bituminous coal (70-86%), and Anthracite has the highest carbon content (> 86%).

options.text: Peat < Lignite < Bituminous < Anthracite
Anthracite < Bituminous < Lignite < Peat
Lignite < Peat < Bituminous < Anthracite
Peat < Bituminous < Lignite < Anthracite

subject: Science
text: During the fractional distillation of crude petroleum, how are the different constituents separated, and which one remains at the very bottom of the fractionating column?
explanation: Separation is based on the boiling points. Hydrocarbons with higher boiling points condense lower down. Bitumen (asphalt) has the highest boiling point (> 350°C) and remains at the bottom.

options.text: Separated by densities; Kerosene remains at the bottom
Separated by boiling points; Petrol remains at the bottom
Separated by boiling points; Bitumen remains at the bottom
Separated by molecular weights; Liquid petroleum gas remains at the bottom

subject: Science
text: Combustion can be rapid, spontaneous, or explosive. Which of the following is an example of spontaneous combustion?
explanation: Spontaneous combustion is the type of combustion in which a material suddenly bursts into flames without any apparent cause. White phosphorus catches fire in air on its own at room temperature.

options.text: A burning matchstick igniting a gas stove
Burning of white phosphorus in air at room temperature
Ignition of a firecracker during a festival
Burning of LPG in a burner when sparked

subject: Science
text: The calorific value of hydrogen is \\(150000 \\text{ kJ/kg}\\), and that of wood is \\(20000 \\text{ kJ/kg}\\). If a process requires \\(300000 \\text{ kJ}\\) of heat energy, what mass of hydrogen is needed compared to wood?
explanation: Using \\(m = \\text{Energy} / \\text{Calorific Value}\\), we calculate: Hydrogen mass = \\(300000 / 150000 = 2 \\text{ kg}\\), and Wood mass = \\(300000 / 20000 = 15 \\text{ kg}\\).

options.text: \\(2 \\text{ kg}\\) of hydrogen and \\(15 \\text{ kg}\\) of wood
\\(1.5 \\text{ kg}\\) of hydrogen and \\(30 \\text{ kg}\\) of wood
\\(5 \\text{ kg}\\) of hydrogen and \\(10 \\text{ kg}\\) of wood
\\(10 \\text{ kg}\\) of hydrogen and \\(100 \\text{ kg}\\) of wood

subject: Science
text: During the electrolysis of copper sulphate solution using copper electrodes, what happens to the concentration of copper sulphate in the electrolyte?
explanation: Copper ions from the solution deposit onto the cathode, while an equal amount of copper dissolves from the copper anode into the solution. Thus, the concentration of copper sulphate in the electrolyte remains constant.

options.text: It decreases steadily as copper is deposited on the cathode
It increases steadily as copper is dissolved from the anode
It remains constant
It turns colorless because of chemical decomposition

subject: Science
text: A student wants to electroplate a copper key with silver. How should the student set up the electrodes and the electrolyte?
explanation: In electroplating, the object to be coated (copper key) must be the cathode (negative electrode), the metal to be deposited (pure silver) must be the anode (positive electrode), and the electrolyte must contain ions of the coating metal (silver nitrate).

options.text: Anode: Copper key; Cathode: Pure silver rod; Electrolyte: Copper sulphate solution
Anode: Pure silver rod; Cathode: Copper key; Electrolyte: Silver nitrate solution
Anode: Pure silver rod; Cathode: Copper key; Electrolyte: Copper sulphate solution
Anode: Copper key; Cathode: Pure silver rod; Electrolyte: Silver nitrate solution

subject: Science
text: A heavy wooden crate is being pushed across a floor. What type of friction opposes its motion once it starts moving, and how does it compare to the friction before it started moving?
explanation: Once the crate starts moving, the interlocking between microscopic irregularities is less, resulting in sliding friction, which is slightly smaller than the static friction required to start the motion.

options.text: Sliding friction, which is slightly smaller than static friction
Static friction, which is larger than sliding friction
Rolling friction, which is larger than sliding friction
Sliding friction, which is twice the static friction

subject: Science
text: Why do mountaineers sometimes experience nosebleeds at high altitudes?
explanation: At high altitudes, the atmospheric pressure decreases. The pressure of the blood inside the body is greater than the external atmospheric pressure, causing delicate blood capillaries in the nose to rupture.

options.text: Because the high concentration of oxygen increases blood pressure
Because the atmospheric pressure decreases, becoming lower than the internal blood pressure
Because the rapid heartbeat at high altitudes thins the blood
Because the extreme cold freezes the blood vessels in the nasal passage

subject: Science
text: The frictional force exerted by fluids is called drag. Which set of factors determines the magnitude of drag on an object moving through a fluid?
explanation: The fluid friction or drag depends on the speed of the object relative to the fluid, the physical shape of the object, and the viscosity (nature) of the fluid.

options.text: Only the speed of the object and the mass of the object
The speed of the object relative to the fluid, the shape of the object, and the nature of the fluid
Only the color of the object, the density of the fluid, and temperature
The volume of the object, the atmospheric pressure, and the gravitational force

subject: Science
text: Lubricants are applied between moving machine parts to reduce friction. Why can lubricants never reduce the force of friction to zero?
explanation: No surface is perfectly smooth. Microscopic irregularities exist on every surface, and some interlocking will always occur even with a thin film of lubricant between them.

options.text: Because lubricants chemically react with metal to produce new irregularities
Because no surface is perfectly smooth and microscopic irregularities still interlock to some extent
Because the lubricant itself exerts a strong magnetic attraction between the surfaces
Because lubricants increase the normal force acting on the surfaces

subject: Science
text: If a guitar string is plucked harder, what physical characteristic of the sound wave changes, and how does it affect our perception of the sound?
explanation: Plucking the string harder increases the energy of vibration, which increases the amplitude of the sound wave, making the sound louder.

options.text: The frequency increases, making the sound higher in pitch
The amplitude increases, making the sound louder
The speed of the sound wave increases, making it reach our ears faster
The wavelength decreases, making the sound softer

subject: Science
text: A person standing at a distance from a tall cliff claps and hears the echo after \\(0.4 \\text{ s}\\). If the speed of sound in air is \\(340 \\text{ m/s}\\), how far is the person from the cliff?
explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, covering twice the distance. Distance is calculated as: \\(d = (v \\times t) / 2 = (340 \\text{ m/s} \\times 0.4 \\text{ s}) / 2 = 68 \\text{ m}\\).

subject: Science
text: How do primary seismic waves (P-waves) and secondary seismic waves (S-waves) differ in their transmission through different states of matter?
explanation: P-waves are longitudinal waves that can travel through both solid and liquid layers of the earth, whereas S-waves are transverse waves that can only propagate through solids.

options.text: P-waves travel only through liquids; S-waves travel only through solids
P-waves travel through both solids and liquids; S-waves travel only through solids
Both P-waves and S-waves travel only through liquid magma
S-waves travel through both solids and liquids; P-waves travel only through gases

subject: Science
text: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror at an angle of incidence of \\(30^\\circ\\). If the mirror is rotated by \\(10^\\circ\\) about an axis lying in its plane, what are the possible new angles of reflection?
explanation: If the mirror is rotated by \\(10^\\circ\\), the normal to the mirror also rotates by \\(10^\\circ\\). Depending on the direction of rotation, the new angle of incidence (and thus reflection) will be either \\(30^\\circ - 10^\\circ = 20^\\circ\\) or \\(30^\\circ + 10^\\circ = 40^\\circ\\).

options.text: Only \\(30^\\circ\\)
Either \\(20^\\circ\\) or \\(40^\\circ\\)
Only \\(40^\\circ\\)
Either \\(15^\\circ\\) or \\(45^\\circ\\)

subject: Science
text: A person can see nearby objects clearly but struggles to focus on distant objects. What is this vision defect called, and how is it corrected?
explanation: Myopia (nearsightedness) occurs when the light rays focus in front of the retina rather than on it. It is corrected using a concave (diverging) lens to shift the focus back onto the retina.

options.text: Hypermetropia, corrected using a convex lens
Myopia, corrected using a concave lens
Presbyopia, corrected using a cylindrical lens
Myopia, corrected using a convex lens
